title: Keyboard menu selection jumps beneath a stationary pointer
symptoms: Opening or navigating a menu by keyboard unexpectedly changes the active command.
A submenu closes without intentional pointer movement.
cause: Layout can place a new menu item beneath the resting pointer and emit a pointerover event that steals keyboard ownership.
minimal_fix: Retain keyboard input ownership until pointer coordinates actually change; restore intentional pointer navigation and press-and-drag activation on genuine movement.

regression_cases.name: stationary pointer preserves keyboard submenu ownership; movement resumes pointer navigation

limitations: Applies to integrations of the v1 API, not a declaration that every v1 menu is broken. Keep the pointer parked over the menu during the regression.

title: Closed dialog cannot reopen immediately
symptoms: Closing and immediately opening the same dialog leaves it invisible or ignored.
A completed dialog still owns an application stack or pending promise.
cause: Application cleanup waits for a later native close event while commands already observe stale open state.
minimal_fix: Call one idempotent finish path synchronously from the application close operation; remove the stack entry, settle callers, update inert regions, and restore logical focus. Retain native close as a fallback.

regression_cases.name: dialog close settles immediately, permits synchronous reopen and restores opener focus

limitations: The consumer must settle its own promises and command guards. The generic dialog cannot infer document-specific completion semantics.

title: Held Escape closes a lower dialog unexpectedly
symptoms: One held Escape dismisses a confirmation and then the dialog underneath.
Nested close handling returns focus to the wrong opener.
cause: Repeated keyboard input or event propagation is handled again after the top dialog has been removed.
minimal_fix: Let only the top dialog handle the current Escape and consume it; ignore repeated Escape until a new key press, and restore the correct opener when the top entry settles.

regression_cases.name: nested dialogs consume one Escape and ignore repeated Escape on the lower dialog

limitations: Verify native cancellation and application-managed dialogs in the target host. Focus behavior changes when an opener has been removed.

title: Splitter cannot be operated by keyboard or escapes pane bounds
symptoms: A pointer drag collapses a pane beyond its declared minimum.
The divider can only be moved by dragging.
cause: Pointer-only movement bypasses a shared bounded value model, or the focusable separator does not expose and operate its range.
minimal_fix: Use one clamped value update for keyboard and pointer changes; expose separator name, orientation, controls, and values. Track capture and pointer cancellation without leaving a stuck drag.

regression_cases.name: splitter keyboard and pointer resizing stay within both pane bounds

limitations: APG splitter review is incomplete. Choose pane minima and collapse policy for the consumer; this record does not prove screen-reader support.

title: Tree disclosure keys lose the hierarchy
symptoms: Right/Left do not expand or reach the logical child/parent.
Rebuilding a branch loses focused item identity.
cause: Focus order is derived from unrelated application commands or stale DOM positions rather than the visible hierarchy.
minimal_fix: Keep stable node IDs, owned child groups, truthful expansion state, and visible-node order; use Right/Left for expand/child/collapse/parent and Up/Down for visible siblings and descendants.

regression_cases.name: tree arrows expand, enter a child and return to the logical parent

limitations: Selection and activation policy remain explicit consumer choices. Archived layer-panel behavior is an example, not a general tree contract.

title: Toolbar keys interfere with native controls or skip toggles
symptoms: Keyboard users cannot reach the toolbar controls.
Arrow keys or Space unexpectedly trigger workspace commands.
Toggle visuals disagree with aria-pressed.
cause: The toolbar or application intercepts keys without recognizing the focused control, or roving focus and pressed state drift from the control model.
minimal_fix: Maintain one reachable toolbar tab stop, skip disabled controls deliberately, expose pressed state from the same model as the visual state, and reserve text/value editing keys before application shortcuts run.

regression_cases.name: toolbar arrows skip disabled controls and exclusive toggles expose pressed state

limitations: The available case covers toolbar navigation and toggles. Consumers must also exercise native text fields, sliders, Space activation, and application shortcut routing.

title: Spin button steps from a stale numeric value
symptoms: A typed value is discarded when an increase/decrease button is pressed.
Stepping commits twice or produces the wrong undo order.
cause: The step button preserves focus and prevents blur, so the pending text draft has not reached the numeric model before stepping.
minimal_fix: Parse and settle the pending draft explicitly before applying a step; clamp through one value path, emit one commit per logical action, and keep native text editing intact.

regression_cases.name: bounded numbers commit typed drafts before stepping and clamp to declared range

limitations: Decimal precision, invalid-input policy, and undo integration are consumer responsibilities. Other pending fields need their own explicit settling policy.

title: Renderer has broader native privileges than required
symptoms: Renderer code can invoke arbitrary IPC channels or Node APIs.
Unexpected navigation loads content with native privileges.
cause: Node integration, disabled isolation, an unrestricted bridge, or unchecked IPC/navigation makes the privilege boundary broader than the application needs.
minimal_fix: Use isolation and sandboxing, keep Node integration disabled for remote content, expose specific validated preload methods, validate IPC senders, and deny unexpected navigation and window creation.

regression_cases.name: host rejects an untrusted IPC sender, arbitrary channel, navigation, and new-window URL

limitations: Requires a consumer Electron integration test and threat-specific review. No security compatibility or native runtime test is claimed by this catalog.

title: Save-and-Close discards edits made during a pending save
symptoms: The dirty marker disappears although edits occurred after serialization.
Save-and-Close closes after writing an older revision.
cause: Save completion marks the current model clean instead of recording only the revision that was serialized.
minimal_fix: Capture revision identity with the serialized bytes, mark that revision saved only after success, keep subsequent revisions dirty, and recheck dirty state before closing.

regression_cases.name: edit while native save is pending keeps the new revision dirty and prevents Save-and-Close

limitations: The consuming app must implement the revision and write protocol. A close-cancellation API alone does not provide asynchronous save safety.

title: Clean Electron launch misses generated assets
symptoms: An app works in a developer checkout but fails to launch in a clean test or package.
A generated icon or other ignored input is missing.
cause: The test launches Electron directly and bypasses the npm lifecycle hook that normally generates prerequisites.
minimal_fix: Generate declared build inputs explicitly before direct launch and packaging, then verify the complete resource tree in a clean fixture.

regression_cases.name: clean checkout generates required ignored inputs before direct Electron launch

limitations: Do not copy a consumer’s older build workaround without checking its current delivery command. The catalog has not run native packaging.

title: A 1:1 preview changes meaning with display scale
symptoms: One source pixel occupies multiple physical pixels despite a physical 1:1 promise.
Moving the window to another display changes preview sharpness or mapping.
cause: The preview equates CSS pixels with physical display pixels or does not update after devicePixelRatio changes.
minimal_fix: Define the 1:1 promise. For physical mapping, size CSS content from raster dimensions times zoom divided by devicePixelRatio, then update when that ratio changes and verify the real host.

regression_cases.name: physical 1:1 raster preview updates after DPR changes and preserves the advertised mapping

limitations: The formula is integration guidance for a physical-pixel promise. A CSS-pixel promise uses different dimensions; fractional rasterization still needs visual inspection.

title: Short windows hide essential actions
symptoms: OK, Cancel, or Apply is clipped at increased display scale.
Scrolling the form also scrolls essential actions out of reach.
cause: The form and footer share an unconstrained scrolling region, or flex/grid children refuse to shrink.
minimal_fix: Keep a constrained scrolling body and a fixed action footer, give nested flex/grid children min-height/min-width zero where appropriate, and choose a usable minimum or reachable fallback.

regression_cases.name: short and narrow windows at supported display scales keep action buttons visible and clickable

limitations: Requires layout and pointer checks in the consumer. A single full-size screenshot does not verify short-window reachability.
